reference.source: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease (OMMBID) / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive single-enzyme peroxisomal defect caused by ACOX1 mutations, in which peroxisome assembly is intact but the first step of peroxisomal fatty-acid beta-oxidation fails
Presents in infancy with hypotonia, seizures, and developmental delay followed by regression, clinically resembling neonatal adrenoleukodystrophy hence the label pseudoneonatal adrenoleukodystrophy

Very-long-chain fatty acids (VLCFA) accumulate in plasma, providing a key screening abnormality, whereas bile acids and plerodenic phytanic/pristanic acids are typically normal because those pathways use different oxidases
White-matter demyelination and hearing and visual impairment develop as the disease advances

Because peroxisome biogenesis is normal, some markers seen in Zellweger-spectrum disorders (very high plasma phytanic acid, abnormal plasmalogens) may be unremarkable, so an isolated VLCFA elevation should prompt consideration of a single-enzyme defect
Diagnosis is confirmed by ACOX1 molecular testing and functional studies; care is supportive with no established disease-modifying therapy
reference.pathophysiology: Acyl-CoA oxidase deficiency is a peroxisomal single-enzyme disorder in which ACOX1 mutations abolish straight-chain acyl-CoA oxidase, the enzyme catalysing the first and rate-limiting oxidation step in peroxisomal beta-oxidation of very-long-chain fatty acids. Because peroxisomes are assembled normally, only this pathway is blocked, so VLCFA accumulate in plasma and tissues while bile-acid and branched-chain (phytanic/pristanic) processing is relatively preserved. Accumulated lipids are neurotoxic, driving progressive cerebral and cerebellar demyelination, neuronal loss, and the associated regression, seizures, and sensory impairment.
additionalDifferentials: D-bifunctional protein deficiency (another single-enzyme peroxisomal beta-oxidation defect)
Other leukodystrophies presenting with infantile regression
Mitochondrial encephalopathies with seizures and hypotonia
Congenital or early-infantile epileptic encephalopathies of other cause
additionalInvestigations: Plasma very-long-chain fatty acid profile (elevated C26:0 and ratios)
ACOX1 gene sequencing to confirm the molecular diagnosis
Plasma phytanic and pristanic acids and bile-acid intermediates to distinguish from broader peroxisomal defects
Brain MRI to characterise the demyelinating leukodystrophy pattern
Fibroblast studies of peroxisomal beta-oxidation and immunofluorescence confirming normal peroxisome assembly
Auditory and visual evoked potentials to document sensory involvement
redFlags: Developmental regression with seizures after an initial period of near-normal development
Rapidly progressive white-matter disease on neuroimaging
Emergent loss of hearing and vision indicating advancing neurodegeneration
Intractable epilepsy requiring escalation of anticonvulsant management
reference.prognosis: The condition is progressive and usually fatal in childhood after a period of neurological regression, though the age of decline varies. There is no curative treatment, and management focuses on seizure control, nutrition, and supportive multidisciplinary care.
pitfalls: Assuming a normal peroxisome-biogenesis screen excludes a peroxisomal disorder, missing an isolated single-enzyme defect
Confusing the phenotype with X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy and delaying autosomal recessive genetic testing
Failing to repeat or extend the VLCFA and enzyme testing when clinical suspicion is high
Overlooking sensory (hearing and visual) impairment that affects developmental support
